=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. There is no talk.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. 5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told

From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. [user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. records.prompt:
[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 4, Dirac. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

There is no talk.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

[user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. [user]
=== Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised) ===

SETUP. With P players, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12 x P, each number once. It is shuffled and each player is dealt 11 cards face down as their hand. The remaining P cards (1 per player) are set aside face down and are never shown. Everyone starts with a game score of 0. The game has P deals of 10 hands each.

INFORMATION. You always see your own hand. Every Weather card becomes public the moment it is played and stays face up in front of whoever played it until the end of that deal. Unplayed cards and set-aside cards are never shown.

START OF EACH DEAL: the Tide deck of cards 1 to 20 is shuffled; every Tide level is set to 15; every player gets 4 lifelines; every Sunk status is cleared. From deal 2 on, each player takes the 10 Weather cards face up in front of them plus the 1 card still in their hand (11 cards) and passes them as a hand to the player on their left; the face-up rows are emptied.

EACH HAND:
1. The next two Tide cards are revealed. The smaller is Low Tide, the larger is High Tide.
2. Every player secretly chooses one Weather card from their hand. All are revealed at once and placed face up in front of whoever played them.
3. The player who played the highest Weather card sets their Tide level to Low Tide. The player who played the second highest sets their Tide level to High Tide. Everyone else keeps their Tide level. Numbers are unique, so there are no ties. Sunk players take part in this step like anyone else.
4. Among players who are NOT Sunk, find the highest Tide level. Every non-Sunk player at that level loses 1 lifeline; a player who must lose a lifeline while at 0 lifelines becomes Sunk instead. Players below that level lose nothing. A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, keeps playing cards and is ignored in this step. If every player is Sunk, nothing happens.
5. All cards played, Tide levels, lifelines and Sunk statuses are announced.

END OF EACH DEAL (after hand 10): each player who is not Sunk adds their remaining lifelines (0 to 4) to their score; each Sunk player subtracts 1; among players who are not Sunk, the player or players with the lowest Tide level each add 1. After each deal every player holds exactly 1 unseen card.

There is no talk.

END. After deal P the game ends. The highest game score wins. If several players tie for the highest score, the tied player with the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal wins. Players still tied on both share the win.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 4. Seats are numbered 1 to 4.
You are seat 3, Curie. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: pass the hands left → reset the seas → your hand → reveal the tide → tide announced → play a weather card → cards go face up → the highest tide loses a lifeline → hand results → end of deal scoring → advance the hand → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  play_a_weather_card answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.
